text: 300 years ago, one place on Earth made about a quarter of everything the whole world produced.
Not Britain. Not China. Not America.
India. Spices. Cotton. Steel. Diamonds.
Ships came from the other side of the planet just to buy what India made.
Riches shop on the planet, and it was always open.
India was so rich, people had a name for it,
Sone Kichidia, the Golden Bird.
And when you're a Golden Bird, everyone wants to catch ya.
Then, in less than 250 years,
that quarter shrank to about 4%.
Ah, someone forgot to lock the shop.
And here's the strange part. This wasn't the first time.
India has been rich and robbed and rebuilt again and again for 5,000 years.
Over that time, this land was ruled by city builders nobody can name,
an emperor who gave up war after one terrible battle,
sultans, moogles, a company, and finally, its own people.
A company? I'll explain later. You will not believe it.
Because, if you look closely, India keeps living the same story.
First, someone stitches the land together, then it shines, the richest place on earth.
Then it shatters into pieces, outsiders march in to take it.
And then, something strange happens.
India absorbs them.
The invaders end up eating its food, speaking its languages, and building its monuments.
Stitch. Shine. Shatter. Absorb. Again and again. So how did one land become the richest place
in the world, lose it all, and start climbing back? Hold on to something. Let's go back
to the very beginning.
